5973-thomas-wingfold-curate-v1:
George MacDonald begins the first volume with wind roaring in every chimney at once, drowning the moan and surge of the woods like a sea. Helen Lingard has stayed in all day, writing to her brother Leopold at Cambridge, and her planned walk in the park has slipped past luncheon into threatening haze.

She has never known a day's illness, and she fears wet weather little more than a young farmer does. Still she pauses at her window above shivering plants and looks out to garden and meadow. Its November weather and a spirited horsewoman set the tone for the curate's story.
thomas-wingfold-curate-v1:
Volume one of George MacDonald's Thomas Wingfold, Curate begins with Helen Lingard watching a November storm from her window. Wind takes every chimney for an organ pipe, and woods moan like a sea. Helen delayed her park walk after writing a long letter to Leopold at Cambridge.

She is healthy, sensible, and seldom merry, yet weather and dress plainly affect her mood. The fireside grows more attractive as rain threatens outside. This record's opening is identical to the opening of the record named without a volume marker, so readers meet the same chapter twice in the library.
